s1.syndrome_frame: Acute onset of bloody diarrhea in a patient with significant weight loss and abdominal tenderness
salient_findings: Bloody diarrhea occurring up to seven times a day
Mild thickening of the wall of the right colon on ultrasound
Diffuse granular and friable mucosa on sigmoidoscopy
Moderately active colitis with cryptitis and crypt abscesses on biopsy
key_facts: Patient is a 34-year-old Palestinian prisoner
Patient is on day 33 of an organized hunger strike
Patient has a one-week history of bloody diarrhea
Patient's BMI reduced from 22.9 kg/m² to 19.4 kg/m²
Patient is pale
Routine laboratory tests are normal
Stool cultures are negative
Clostridium difficile toxin is not present
Ultrasound shows mild thickening of the wall of the right colon
Abdominal CT is normal
Sigmoidoscopy shows continuous diffuse granular and friable mucosa to the ascending colon
Biopsy findings show moderately active colitis with cryptitis and crypt abscesses

shortlist.label: Ulcerative colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Continuous diffuse granular and friable mucosa to the ascending colon, moderately active colitis with cryptitis and crypt abscesses

shortlist.label: Crohn's disease
shortlist.why_kept: Mild thickening of the wall of the right colon, bloody diarrhea, and significant weight loss

shortlist.label: Infectious colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bloody diarrhea and abdominal tenderness, despite negative stool cultures and absence of Clostridium difficile toxin

shortlist.label: Ischemic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Significant weight loss and abdominal tenderness, potentially related to hunger strike

shortlist.label: Microscopic colitis
shortlist.why_kept: Bloody diarrhea and normal abdominal CT, with potential for microscopic inflammation

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms of bloody diarrhea and abdominal tenderness, combined with the endoscopy and biopsy findings of moderately active colitis, are consistent with infectious colitis, particularly in the context of a hunger strike which may lead to malnutrition and increased susceptibility to infections.

rejected.label: Ulcerative colitis
rejected.why: While the biopsy findings could be consistent with ulcerative colitis, the acute onset and the context of a hunger strike make infectious colitis more likely.

rejected.label: Crohn's disease
rejected.why: The lack of peritonitis and the specific findings on sigmoidoscopy and biopsy do not strongly support Crohn's disease.

rejected.label: Ischemic colitis
rejected.why: The patient's age and the absence of risk factors for ischemic colitis, such as cardiovascular disease, make this diagnosis less likely.

rejected.label: Microscopic colitis
rejected.why: The presence of bloody diarrhea and the findings on endoscopy and biopsy are not typical of microscopic colitis, which usually presents with watery diarrhea and normal endoscopic appearance.
